mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return difference from baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months indicates labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE rise > 0.5pp in 3 months), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST) growth and industrial production (INDPRO) decline signal demand-supply mismatch where strong housing demand outpaces manufacturing capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST rises and INDPRO falls, or the interaction term has a negative Rank IC in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a federal funds rate increase (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of high-inflation periods when FEDFUNDS rises, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth is above 2.5% YoY, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp industrial production decline exceeding 2.0% over three months signals manufacturing contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (INDPRO fall > 2.0% in 3 months), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) and retail sales decline (RSAFS) indicate labor market recovery without consumer spending support, signaling weak economic momentum and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises and RSAFS falls, or the interaction term has a negative Rank IC in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 6.0%), employment growth (PAYEMS) signals labor market strengthening that supports consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of high-unemployment periods when PAYEMS rises, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.
